text: The masking version in force in SIT is "MASK-SIT-01", and the mask of a field is the row of that version whose valid_from is the latest on or before the business date.
why: The legacy story, the FSD masking criteria and the sibling stories of this key use "MASK-SIT-01" as the masking version of the SIT environment, while no source read for this work package states the label of the version in force or what happens when a version changes mid-day.
read: RWB-E2-034 sections 3, 4 and 13; FSD P4 A2.5 AC-ALT-P4-005-01, AC-EXC-P4-004-05; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-07
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer and the reference data administrator at the wave-2 masking load
impact: A label and a validity rule only; no role, right or mask value is fixed by it

text: The personal fields of a ledger entry that the mask covers are DF-INT-011 summary and DF-INT-022 contact point, with DF-ACE-076 and DF-ACE-077 behind them, and the same two markers apply to an entry whatever its channel or source.
why: The legacy story requires the contact point to be masked by role and stored as a reference, and REQ-ILG-014 asks for personal data in the ledger to be masked by role; the entry also carries a summary, and no source read for this work package lists which field IDs of the entry the masking rows cover.
read: RWB-E2-034 BR5, REQ-ILG-014, section 10 and section 11; FSD P4 A2.5, AC-ALT-P4-004-01; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule; RWB-P2-E2034-CON entry command; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
confirm: Data steward and Compliance at the masking load; rwb-source-data contract owner on the field IDs of the entry
impact: Adds or removes a field ID from the masked set only; no rule, refusal or test data changes

text: One answered ledger read writes one AC-READ decision record naming the case ID, the field IDs asked and their markers; one refusal writes one AC-DENY record with the area and the right and no case ID.
why: The legacy story and the FSD write one access entry per read of the case record and one per refusal, and name the field IDs and their masked markers, but they do not say whether a read of a page of ledger entries is one entry or one per entry.
read: RWB-E2-034 section 10 and section 12; FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01, AC-EXC-P4-007-04, A2.16; FEAT-ACA-07, FEAT-ACA-08, FEAT-ACA-16
confirm: Internal audit and the platform administrator at the access-log review
impact: A volume and query shape only; the answer, the markers and the refusals are unchanged

text: The decision of this story is served by the existing authorise element of the wave-1 contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON on POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise, and the four rows the Ownership Map gives P4 are its administration operations; the case attributes of an authorise request are the case ID, its owner, its team and its region.
why: The Ownership Map rows of the service list four administration operations and no authorise row, while every sibling story of this key consumes the authorise element at that path from the wave-1 contract; the sources name the scope values but not the attributes a request carries for a case.
read: Recovery Workbench Ownership Map v1 rows for P4; RWB-P4-E1037-CON; FSD P4 A2.14, TSD P4 T6.1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08; sibling stories RWB-P1-E2034-APP, RWB-P2-E2034-CON, RWB-P3-E2034-APP
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access contract owner at contract review
impact: A path and an attribute set only; no rule, criterion or test value changes

text: The access-log page default and maximum and the batch limit of field IDs per answer are parameter rows read through the parameters contract of rwb-case, with their names and values set at build, and the 2 s is the platform standard of the guard client rather than a parameter of this story.
why: The legacy story carries paging on the interaction read and holds no parameter for the access log, and the target moves every bound and timeout to the parameters contract of DP-06; the sources do not name the rows this story needs.
read: RWB-E2-034 sections 12 and 13; FSD P4 A2.16 API-P4-008 page and size; TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-008; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06, DP-11
confirm: Parameter load at wave 2 and the platform resilience standard
impact: No bound or timeout in code; the values are set by data

text: The service runs as "the rwb-access login (DP-02)", one login and one schema for the service, and no shared recovery login is used.
why: One login per service is the platform rule, and the legacy story ran under the shared recovery service identity; the name of the login is not stated in any source read for this work package.
read: RWB-E2-034 section 3 and section 10; TSD P4 T1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-02
confirm: ACE DB team at the schema and login build of the service
impact: A name only; the story never refers to a shared login

text: An agent or service identity that reads the ledger is decided by the same right, scope and mask checks as a person, and its read writes the same AC-READ entry with its own actor reference in place of a person's.
why: NFR-051 and FEAT-ACA-05 require an agent to pass the same role checks as a person and the personal fields to be masked to every agent, while the legacy story names a person as the reader and does not say how an agent's read is logged.
read: RWB-E2-034 section 10; FSD P4 A2.5; TSD P4 T6.1, T6.2; NFR-051
confirm: Solution architect and Compliance at the agent access review
impact: Extends the decision and the record to a non-human actor; no rule or mask value changes
